proof_summary: Since \(2^{10n+2}\equiv4\pmod{66}\), exponent reduction modulo \(66\) gives \(2^{2^{10n+2}+2}+3\equiv2^6+3\equiv0\pmod{67}\). For every prime below \(67\), multiplicative-order periodicity reduces possible divisibility to finitely many residue cases, all of which are excluded, so the exhibited divisor is the smallest prime factor.
